name: Mauritius
tagline: Reef, sugar and the volcanic interior
summary: A volcanic island inside an almost unbroken reef, with a mountainous interior, Black River Gorges, and a culture assembled from India, Africa, France and China in the space of two centuries.

entries.caption: Reef, Sugar and the Volcanic Interior
entries.description: A ring of reef, a green interior of sugar and mountain, and four cultures on one island.
entries.subject: the mountain of Le Morne rising above the lagoon

entries.caption: Lagoon and Gorge
entries.description: Lagoon all the way round, sugar cane across the plain, and gorges cut into the plateau.
entries.subject: the Black River gorges in morning cloud

entries.caption: What the Dodo Left
entries.description: The dodo is gone, but the pink pigeon and the kestrel were both brought back from single figures.
entries.subject: a Mauritius kestrel perched in native forest

entries.caption: Reef, Not Savanna
entries.description: No big game — the wildlife here is the reef, the endemic birds, and the flying foxes at dusk.
entries.subject: fruit bats leaving a roost at dusk

entries.caption: Le Morne and Pieter Both
entries.description: Le Morne Brabant stands 556 metres out of the lagoon, and is walked in a morning.
entries.subject: the summit ridge of Le Morne Brabant above the sea

entries.caption: Chamarel
entries.description: A hundred metres in a single drop, near the seven-coloured earths.
entries.subject: the Chamarel waterfall dropping into forest

entries.caption: Grand Bassin
entries.description: A crater lake and Hindu pilgrimage site, with half a million people walking to it at Maha Shivaratri.
entries.subject: the temple and statues at Grand Bassin crater lake

entries.caption: The Lagoon
entries.description: Inside the reef the water is flat and warm the whole way round the island.
entries.subject: turquoise lagoon and reef break off a Mauritian beach

entries.caption: Black River Gorges
entries.description: The last of the native forest, on the plateau, with trails and endemic birds in it.
entries.subject: native forest in the Black River Gorges

entries.caption: Kite, Dive, Hike
entries.description: Kitesurfing at Le Morne, diving the outer reef, and hiking the gorges and the mountains.
entries.subject: kitesurfers on the lagoon below Le Morne

entries.caption: Four Continents
entries.description: Indian, African, French and Chinese, in one Creole language and one calendar.
entries.subject: a Hindu temple and a church on the same Mauritian street

entries.caption: Creole and Bhojpuri
entries.description: Creole spoken by everyone, Bhojpuri in the villages, and French and English in print.
entries.subject: a village street in the Mauritian sugar country

entries.caption: Dholl Puri and Rougaille
entries.description: Dholl puri off a street cart, rougaille at home, and a fish vindaye that is entirely local.
entries.subject: dholl puri being made at a street cart

entries.caption: Maha Shivaratri and Cavadee
entries.description: Half a million walking to Grand Bassin in February, and Thaipoosam Cavadee in January.
entries.subject: pilgrims walking to Grand Bassin at Maha Shivaratri

entries.caption: Model Ships and Textiles
entries.description: Model shipbuilding, and a textile industry that grew out of the sugar estates.
entries.subject: a model ship being built in a Mauritian workshop

entries.caption: Aapravasi Ghat
entries.description: The immigration depot where half a million indentured labourers first landed.
entries.subject: the stone steps of the Aapravasi Ghat

entries.caption: Le Morne
entries.description: The mountain where escaped slaves lived at the top, and a world heritage site for that reason.
entries.subject: Le Morne Brabant seen from the lagoon

entries.caption: Port Louis
entries.description: A working port and capital, with a market, a waterfront and the Champ de Mars.
entries.subject: the Port Louis waterfront and market

entries.caption: Colonial and Estate
entries.description: The plantation houses of the interior, and the colonial buildings of Port Louis.
entries.subject: a colonial plantation house with a wide veranda

entries.caption: The Central Market
entries.description: Port Louis market in the morning, for vegetables, tea and alouda.
entries.subject: the vegetable stalls of Port Louis central market

entries.caption: Made for Families
entries.description: Flat warm lagoon, no dangerous surf inside the reef, and short drives from anywhere.
entries.subject: children playing in a calm Mauritian lagoon

entries.caption: Kite, Hike, Dive
entries.description: Le Morne's kite lagoon, the Black River trails, and dive sites outside the reef.
entries.subject: hikers on the trail up Le Morne

entries.caption: The Resort Standard
entries.description: The island effectively invented the Indian Ocean resort, and it still does it best.
entries.subject: a resort beach and lagoon in the late afternoon

entries.caption: Bringing Back the Birds
entries.description: The kestrel, the pink pigeon and the echo parakeet were each brought back from near zero.
entries.subject: a pink pigeon in Mauritian native forest

entries.caption: Lagoon Colour
entries.description: The lagoon changes colour every hundred metres, and the aerial work here is the proof.
entries.subject: aerial view of a Mauritian lagoon and reef

entries.caption: Rodrigues
entries.description: Six hundred kilometres east, a tenth the size, and the island Mauritius used to be.
entries.subject: the hills and lagoon of Rodrigues island

entries.caption: Four Cultures, One Lagoon
entries.description: A Hindu festival, a Creole kitchen, a French road name and a Chinese shop, in one street.
entries.subject: a busy multicultural street scene in Port Louis
